title: What a p-value is not
summary: Two activities and three written answers for a methods seminar: build the sampling distribution a p-value is read from, then see what sample size does to the same observed difference.
author: Open Psychology Interactives
intro:
Work through the two activities in order and write your answers to the questions as you go. Bring your answers to the seminar. Nothing you type here is sent anywhere: download or copy your answers at the end.

You will need about 20 minutes.

steps.text: Before you touch anything: two groups of 40 people are drawn from exactly the same population. The true difference between them is zero. **Write down how big a difference between the two group means would surprise you.**

steps.instructions: Run 1,000 studies at the default settings and look at the pile. Then raise *Per group* to 200 without moving anything else, and watch the p-value.

steps.prompt: The observed difference did not change when you raised the sample size. Why did the p-value change?

steps.instructions: Answer the prediction question first. Then find the smallest sample size at which a true effect of the default size is found more often than it is missed.

steps.prompt: In one sentence: what is a p-value conditional on?
A study reports p = .30 and concludes there is no effect. What is wrong with that sentence, and what would you write instead?
